In human cell models unseen in training, silmitasertib plus low-dose interferon raised it roughly 50%, per the developers. Cell tests only; preprint.
milestones.why_it_matters: Antigen presentation is a key immune trigger. A model that proposes a context-specific drug effect that then holds in cells is an early case of AI-guided hypothesis generation in biology.

sources.label: bioRxiv preprint, posted 2025-04-17, revised 2025-10-11 and later

milestones.title: Machine-discovered reinforcement learning rule beats human-designed ones
milestones.summary: DeepMind meta-learned a reinforcement learning update rule from the experience of a population of agents across many environments. The discovered rule, Disco57, scored an interquartile mean of 13.86 on the 57-game Atari benchmark, beating all existing hand-designed rules including MuZero, and reached state of the art on unseen benchmarks such as ProcGen.

before_after.metric: Atari-57 human-normalized IQM score

milestones.why_it_matters: Learning algorithms have been designed by hand for decades. Machines discovering better ones suggests future AI methods may be found automatically from experience.

milestones.title: Fully automated AI lifestyle coach matches human coaches for prediabetes
milestones.summary: In a 368-person randomized noninferiority trial at two US sites led by Johns Hopkins, referral to a fully automated, app-based AI Diabetes Prevention Program met the composite weight, activity and HbA1c goal as often as human-coached programs (31.7% vs 31.9%). More people started the AI program (93.4% vs 82.7%).

before_after.metric: Participants reaching composite prevention goal at 12 months

milestones.why_it_matters: Proven diabetes-prevention coaching is underused because human coaches are scarce. An automated coach that works as well could scale prevention cheaply.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve tested on 67 problems with Tao and Gómez-Serrano
milestones.summary: Bogdan Georgiev, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Terence Tao and Adam Zsolt Wagner ran AlphaEvolve on 67 problems. It rediscovered the best known constructions in most cases, improved several, sometimes generalized finite results into formulas valid for all inputs, and was combined with Deep Think and AlphaProof to generate proofs.
milestones.why_it_matters: A systematic test by leading mathematicians across dozens of problems, mapping where AI search helps and where it does not, instead of one cherry-picked success.

milestones.title: Kosmos AI scientist runs 12-hour autonomous data-driven research campaigns
milestones.summary: Kosmos runs up to 12 hours, reading about 1,500 papers and executing 42,000 lines of code per run, coordinated through a structured world model. Independent scientists judged 79.4% of its report statements accurate; collaborators said a run equalled about six months of their work. Three of seven highlighted discoveries matched findings it had not seen.
milestones.why_it_matters: Staying coherent over hundreds of steps lets an AI pursue a question in depth, so data-rich fields could test far more hypotheses than human teams have time for.

milestones.title: Nanosatellite performs an in-orbit attitude manoeuvre with a learned controller
milestones.summary: On 30 October 2025 the Würzburg 3U nanosatellite InnoCube turned to a target attitude with its reaction wheels under a deep-reinforcement-learning controller trained only in simulation; repeated manoeuvres also worked. The team calls it the first in-orbit demonstration of an AI-based attitude controller and compares it with InnoCube's classical PD controller.

before_after.metric: AI-based satellite attitude control
before_after.after: inertial-pointing manoeuvres in orbit, from 30 October 2025

milestones.why_it_matters: Classical attitude controllers take long to design and are sensitive to model errors. A controller learned in simulation that works on a real spacecraft could cut design time and adapt to changing conditions.
milestones.contested_note: The 'first' claim is the team's own. Tests cover inertial-pointing manoeuvres on one small satellite.

milestones.title: AI control framework runs five live fusion experiments on the DIII-D tokamak
milestones.summary: PPPL and Princeton's PACMAN framework links machine-learning predictors and controllers in a loop that typically runs in about 20 milliseconds. In five DIII-D experiments it let a reinforcement-learning agent run the heating, steered all six microwave gyrotrons at once, controlled density and rotation, and predicted a tearing instability ~200 ms ahead to avoid it.

before_after.metric: Warning before a tearing-mode instability
before_after.before: conventional control acts only after onset

milestones.why_it_matters: Fusion plasmas need many actuators adjusted faster than people can react. A shared, safety-limited framework lets several AI models predict and control a real tokamak together.
ai_systems: PACMAN (Prediction And Control using MAchiNe learning)

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning sets new kissing-number records in dimensions 25 to 31
milestones.summary: PackingStar, a reinforcement learning system that treats the kissing number problem as a two-player game of filling in tables of cosines between sphere centres, beat the best known lower bounds in every dimension from 25 to 31, for example from 197,048 to 197,056 touching spheres in 25 dimensions and from 232,874 to 238,350 in 31.

before_after.metric: Kissing number lower bound in 31 dimensions

milestones.why_it_matters: The kissing number, how many equal spheres can touch a central one, is known exactly in only six dimensions; the old records in dimensions 25 to 31 all came from one Leech-lattice construction.
organizations: Shanghai Academy of AI for Science
milestones.contested_note: The configurations are explicit and checkable but not yet peer-reviewed. The 13-dimensional 1,146 beats only the 1,130 rational construction of 1971, not the 1,154 record. The September 2026 revision reports 15 improved bounds across kissing-type problems.

sources.label: Ma et al., Finding Kissing Numbers with Game-theoretic Reinforcement Learning, arXiv:2511.13391

milestones.title: Robot model learns from its own practice, doubling throughput on hard tasks
milestones.summary: Physical Intelligence trained its vision-language-action model π*0.6 with Recap, reinforcement learning from demonstrations, expert corrections and the robot's own attempts. On some of the hardest tasks, practice more than doubled throughput and roughly halved failure rates; robots made espresso from 5:30am to 11:30pm and folded 50 novel laundry items in a new home.

before_after.metric: Successful tasks per hour, diverse laundry and espresso
before_after.after: more than 2x, with failure rate roughly halved

milestones.why_it_matters: Robots trained only by imitation compound small errors. Learning from their own mistakes and corrections is a step toward reliable work outside the lab.
ai_systems: π*0.6 vision-language-action model trained with Recap
milestones.contested_note: Company results on its own tasks and robots, compared with its own baselines; not peer reviewed.

milestones.title: GPT-5 case studies include four new maths results, among them Erdős #848
milestones.summary: OpenAI and academic collaborators documented GPT-5 in live research, including four new, human-verified mathematics results. In one, GPT-5 Pro supplied an idea that, with earlier online comments, let Mehtaab Sawhney settle Erdős problem #848: for large N, the numbers ≡ 7 (mod 25) form a largest set in which no product-plus-one ab+1 is squarefree.
milestones.why_it_matters: It records, with transcripts, where a general-purpose model actually moved research forward and where it failed, giving mathematicians concrete evidence rather than anecdotes.
milestones.contested_note: The authors call the new results modest in scope. For #848, GPT-5's own attempts at a full proof had numerous errors; Sawhney turned its idea into the proof.

sources.label: Bubeck et al., Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5, arXiv:2511.16072
OpenAI, Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5 (2025-11-20)

milestones.title: Deep learning forecasts aftershocks in seconds with skill similar to ETAS
milestones.summary: British Geological Survey, Edinburgh and Padua researchers trained deep-learning models on earthquake catalogues from California, New Zealand, Italy, Japan and Greece to forecast how many aftershocks follow magnitude 4+ quakes over 24 hours, and where. On Southern California and Italy tests they matched the standard ETAS model, in seconds instead of hours to days.

before_after.metric: Time to produce a 24-hour aftershock forecast
before_after.before: hours to days (ETAS simulations on a mid-range computer)
before_after.after: seconds, with comparable skill on two test regions

milestones.why_it_matters: Aftershocks can be deadlier than the main quake. Forecasts available almost at once could guide rescue, evacuation and building checks while a seismic crisis is still unfolding.
milestones.contested_note: Exploratory study (titled 'Towards...'): comparable skill to ETAS was shown on Southern California and Italy test sets only, and the models are not yet used operationally.

sources.label: Dervisi et al., Earth, Planets and Space 77:185, 2025-11-25

milestones.title: Randomized trial: ambient AI scribes reduce clinician work exhaustion
milestones.summary: In a 24-week stepped-wedge trial, 66 UW Health practitioners in Wisconsin and Illinois were randomized to staggered starts with Abridge, an ambient AI that drafts visit notes. It drafted 38% of 71,487 notes; work exhaustion fell 0.44 points (five-point scale) and note time 0.36 hours a day, with no loss of note quality.

before_after.metric: Time spent on notes per practitioner per day

milestones.why_it_matters: Paperwork drives physician burnout and takes time from patients. Randomized evidence, not just surveys, shows generative AI can return some time, though trials were short and gains varied by product.
ai_systems: Microsoft DAX Copilot and Nabla (companion UCLA trial)
organizations: University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health
milestones.contested_note: Results differ by product: a companion UCLA randomized trial in the same NEJM AI issue (238 physicians) found Nabla cut time-in-note 9.5% while Microsoft DAX showed no significant change; burnout measures there were secondary end points.

milestones.title: Aristotle proves a version of Erdős problem #124 in Lean on its own
milestones.summary: Working only from a formal statement in the Formal Conjectures project, Harmonic's Aristotle spent six hours on a Lean proof that, whenever 1/(d₁−1)+…+1/(d_r−1) ≥ 1, every whole number is a sum of one number per base dᵢ with base-dᵢ digits all 0 or 1. Boris Alexeev posted it on 29 November 2025.
milestones.why_it_matters: An early case of an AI prover settling a listed problem end to end, and a lesson in how loosely stated problems can make 'solved' claims misleading.
milestones.contested_note: Thomas Bloom (forum, 30 Nov 2025): Aristotle solved 'a' version, with an olympiad-style proof, but not 'the' version; the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Li form, which excludes the digit 1s, remains open. The original formal statement also had a typo that weakened it, which Alexeev corrected.

milestones.title: Stroke AI software rollout tied to doubled thrombectomy rates in England
milestones.summary: Across all 107 English NHS stroke hospitals (452,952 admissions, 2019-2023), the 26 sites that systematically adopted Brainomix 360 Stroke saw thrombectomy rates rise from 2.3% to 4.6%, versus 1.6% to 2.6% elsewhere. Patients whose scans were read with the AI had higher odds of thrombectomy (OR 1.57). Observational; some authors work for Brainomix.

before_after.metric: Thrombectomy rate at AI-adopting hospitals

milestones.why_it_matters: Clot removal saves brain function but depends on fast expert scan reading. AI that flags blocked vessels may widen access across a national system, though observational data cannot prove causation.
organizations: Health Innovation Oxford and Thames Valley

milestones.title: AxiomProver writes Lean proofs for all 12 Putnam 2025 problems
milestones.summary: Axiom's AxiomProver received the Putnam 2025 problems section by section from an official proctor on 6 December 2025 and autonomously produced Lean proofs for all 12, eight of them before the exam closed. Axiom released the machine-checked proofs with commentary on 8 January 2026.
milestones.why_it_matters: Every answer is machine-checked, so no human grader is needed to trust it. A formal prover handled a full, unseen, hard exam under time pressure.
milestones.contested_note: Timing (8 of 12 within the exam window) is Axiom's own account, and a technical report was still to come. Some proofs are long and brute-force, such as a 1,061-line case analysis for B4.

sources.label: Axiom, From Seeing Why to Checking Everything (2026-01-08)

milestones.title: AlphaQubit 2 decodes surface and colour quantum codes in real time
milestones.summary: Google's AlphaQubit 2 neural decoder reached near-optimal logical error rates for surface and colour codes in realistic-noise simulations and matched AlphaQubit 1 on Willow chip data. It decoded in under 1 µs per cycle on commercial accelerators: the surface code up to distance 11 and, a first, the colour code up to distance 9.

before_after.metric: real-time colour-code decoding
before_after.after: under 1 µs per cycle up to distance 9

milestones.why_it_matters: Superconducting qubits are measured about a million times a second, so decoders must be fast and accurate. Real-time neural decoding removes the speed limit of the first AlphaQubit.

milestones.title: Equational Theories Project settles all 22 million magma law implications
milestones.summary: A Terence Tao-led online collaboration launched in September 2024 settled all 22,028,942 implications between the 4,694 simplest equational laws for magmas, combining human proofs with automated theorem provers such as Vampire and Prover9/Mace4, all checked in Lean. Large language models played only a minor role.

before_after.metric: Implications resolved among 4,694 laws

milestones.why_it_matters: A model for large-scale mathematics: many contributors plus automated provers, with a proof checker guaranteeing each of millions of results.

milestones.title: AI tools help pin down the exact answer to Erdős problem #1026
milestones.summary: An ambiguous 1971 Erdős question on monotone subsequence sums was made precise and answered online. Harmonic's Aristotle proved the square case in Lean on 7 December 2025, AlphaEvolve data suggested a formula for every length, and an AI literature search found a 2024 packing result that completed it. Terence Tao wrote up the full proof.
milestones.why_it_matters: A documented case of AI tools fitting into open collaborative mathematics, with formal proving, numerical exploration and literature search each checked by people.
milestones.contested_note: The square case Aristotle proved was already in Tidor, Wang and Yang (2016), whom erdosproblems.com credits with the first proof; Tao traces its packing idea to Seidenberg (1959). The final assembly relies on cited results and was not formalized.

sources.label: Terence Tao, The story of Erdős problem #1026 (2025-12-08)

milestones.title: FDA qualifies its first AI drug-development tool, for liver biopsy scoring
milestones.summary: The FDA qualified AIM-NASH, PathAI's cloud AI that scores liver biopsies for fat, inflammation, ballooning and scarring, for MASH drug trials. Pathologists accept or reject every AI score. Validation showed AI-assisted reads agreed with expert consensus as well as individual pathologists did. Europe's medicines agency had qualified the tool earlier in 2025.
milestones.why_it_matters: MASH drug trials hinge on biopsy scores that pathologists often disagree on. A regulator-qualified AI reader can make trial end points more consistent and cheaper, and sets a precedent for AI in drug development.

sources.label: PathAI press release (notes prior EMA qualification), 2025-12-09

milestones.title: Drug flagged by an AI cell-imaging screen shrinks polyps in hereditary disease
milestones.summary: Recursion reported phase 1b/2 TUPELO data for REC-4881, a MEK1/2 inhibitor its AI-driven cell-imaging screen flagged for familial adenomatous polyposis. Median polyp burden fell 43% after 12 weeks on drug (12 patients) and stood 53% below baseline at week 25, 12 weeks after stopping (11 patients). Grade 3 side effects affected 15.8% of 19 patients.
milestones.why_it_matters: Familial adenomatous polyposis has no approved drug and often ends in colon removal. Small, open-label, company-reported data suggest AI phenotypic screens can repurpose existing molecules for rare diseases.

milestones.title: GPT-5.2 Pro proves Gaussian maximum likelihood improves with more data
milestones.summary: Mark Sellke and Steven Yin report that GPT-5.2 Pro variants derived every result in their paper, the first nontrivial proofs that the maximum likelihood estimator's average log-loss never worsens with more data, for Gaussians with unknown covariance and Gamma variables with unknown scale. The Gaussian case was flagged open; humans only prompted and checked.
milestones.why_it_matters: Learning theorists had shown that extra data can hurt some learners; settling the textbook Gaussian case shows when the basic intuition holds, and the proofs came from the model.
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer-reviewed; OpenAI says external experts reviewed the proofs.

sources.label: Sellke and Yin, On Learning-Curve Monotonicity for Maximum Likelihood Estimators, arXiv:2512.10220
OpenAI, Advancing science and math with GPT-5.2 (2025-12-11)

milestones.title: Two computer-designed 20 kN methane rocket engines hot-fired within three weeks
milestones.summary: LEAP 71 says its Noyron computational engineering model autonomously designed a bell-nozzle engine and a full-scale aerospike, each 20 kN, burning methane and liquid oxygen, and that specification to first flame took under three weeks. The bell engine ran above 93% combustion efficiency; the aerospike reached its 50 bar chamber pressure in a single burn.
milestones.why_it_matters: Engine design is slow, iterative expert work. Generating working hardware directly from a specification could shorten development cycles for propulsion and other complex machines.
milestones.contested_note: Company announcement only. Noyron encodes physics and engineering rules rather than learning from data, and the aerospike ran once because of start-up transient problems.

milestones.title: AI agent places first ahead of 804 humans in an AtCoder Heuristic Contest
milestones.summary: Sakana AI's ALE-Agent, a system making about 4,800 calls to GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro, entered the four-hour AtCoder Heuristic Contest 058 on 14 December 2025 by special permission, unrated, and took first place among 804 human entrants with an approach that beat the problem setter's intended solution. It cost about US$1,300.
milestones.why_it_matters: Heuristic contests reward open-ended optimisation, close to real engineering problems like scheduling and routing, rather than puzzles with known answers.

sources.label: AtCoder contest history for ALE-Agent's account (rank 1 in AHC058)

milestones.title: Gemini tool checks STOC 2026 papers for proof errors before submission
milestones.summary: STOC 2026 offered authors optional, private feedback from a Gemini Deep Think tool tuned for mathematical rigour. Over 80% of papers submitted by the experiment's end opted in. More than 100 authors answered a survey and 97% of those quoted found it helpful; one said it caught a bug that made their proof entirely incorrect.
milestones.why_it_matters: Proofs in theory papers are long, and reviewers rarely check every step. An automated rigour check before submission catches errors when they are cheapest to fix.
ai_systems: Paper Assistant Tool (PAT), built on an advanced Gemini 2.5 Deep Think
milestones.contested_note: Results come from Google's own survey of consenting respondents, with no count of errors found. Reviews went to authors only, not the program committee (STOC 2026 programme page).

milestones.title: AI search of Hubble's archive finds over 1,300 anomalies, 800 undocumented
milestones.summary: ESA's David O'Ryan and Pablo Gómez ran AnomalyMatch, a semi-supervised, active-learning neural network, over 99.6 million image cutouts from the Hubble Legacy Archive in about two and a half days. Inspecting its top-ranked sources, they confirmed more than 1,300 anomalies, over 800 previously undocumented, including 86 new candidate lenses and 18 jellyfish galaxies.

before_after.metric: Systematic anomaly search of the whole Hubble Legacy Archive
before_after.before: never done; anomalies found by hand or by chance

milestones.why_it_matters: Rare objects such as lenses and merging galaxies test ideas about dark matter and galaxy growth. Fast AI triage makes it practical to mine old archives and coming surveys like Euclid and Rubin.

milestones.title: Machine-learning screen leads to two new kagome superconductors
milestones.summary: The SuperC consortium used machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening plus first-principles calculations to pick kagome-lattice compounds. Rice University then made YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2 and measured bulk superconductivity, with critical temperatures of 0.81 K and 0.95 K and nearly 100% superconducting volume fractions.

before_after.metric: Known superconductivity in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2
before_after.after: bulk superconductors, Tc 0.81 K and 0.95 K

milestones.why_it_matters: Superconductor discovery is still mostly trial and error. A screen that cheaply narrows candidates before synthesis could scale the search, though these temperatures are far from practical.
milestones.contested_note: Gaggl et al. (arXiv:2512.09314, 2025-12-10; Physica Scripta, 2026) independently reported bulk superconductivity in YRu3B2 (Tc 0.7 K) six days earlier, without machine learning.

sources.label: Albu Mustaf et al., Physical Review Research 8, 023308, 2026-06-17

milestones.title: AI-read ECGs double new diagnoses of advanced liver disease in primary care
milestones.summary: Mayo Clinic cluster-randomized 98 primary-care teams; in half, clinicians were alerted when a model reading routine ECGs flagged likely advanced chronic liver disease. Among 15,596 adults, new diagnoses of advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis within 180 days were 1.0% with alerts versus 0.5% without (odds ratio 2.09). Clinician follow-up of alerts was uneven.

before_after.metric: New advanced chronic liver disease diagnoses within 180 days

milestones.why_it_matters: Cirrhosis is often found only after complications. Using a cheap test that patients already get to flag hidden liver disease could bring earlier treatment at almost no extra cost.
ai_systems: ECG-based machine learning model for advanced chronic liver disease

milestones.title: NOAA puts AI global forecast models and a hybrid AI-physics ensemble into use
milestones.summary: NOAA deployed three AI-based global systems built from a fine-tuned GraphCast: AIGFS, whose 16-day forecast uses 0.3% of the GFS's computing; a 31-member AI ensemble with early skill gains of 18-24 hours; and a 62-member hybrid AI-physics ensemble that beat both on most metrics. NOAA notes weaker hurricane intensity forecasts in version 1.

before_after.metric: Computing for a 16-day global forecast

milestones.why_it_matters: The US national weather service now runs AI forecasts operationally, and blending AI and physics ensembles points to a way of keeping the strengths of both.

milestones.title: Scientists using LLMs post 24-89% more papers; polished prose loses its signal
milestones.summary: Cornell and Berkeley researchers analysed 2.1 million preprints, 28,000 peer-review reports and 246 million document accesses. Scientists who began drafting with large language models raised paper output by 23.7% to 89.3%, depending on field and background. LLM use reversed the link between complex writing and paper quality, and adopters cited more diverse, younger work.

before_after.metric: Paper output after adopting LLMs for drafting
before_after.after: +23.7% to +89.3%, depending on field and author background

milestones.why_it_matters: Journals, funders and hiring committees use output and writing quality as signals of merit. Measuring how AI changes both shows those signals need rethinking.
ai_systems: Large language models (ChatGPT and others), detected by text analysis
milestones.contested_note: LLM use is inferred from text, and the associations are observational, not causal.

milestones.title: MASAI trial: AI-supported mammography finds more cancers, misses no more
milestones.summary: Sweden's MASAI trial randomized 105,934 women to AI-supported screening (Transpara triaging scans to single or double reading) or standard double reading. AI found 29% more cancers (6.4 vs 5.0 per 1,000) with 44% less reading; interval cancers were non-inferior (1.55 vs 1.76 per 1,000) and sensitivity rose from 73.8% to 80.5%.

before_after.metric: Screening sensitivity

milestones.why_it_matters: Finding more cancers only helps if no more are missed between screens. A large randomized trial showing both, with far less radiologist time, is strong evidence for real screening programs.

sources.label: The Lancet (interval cancers, primary endpoint), 2026-01-31 issue

milestones.title: Generative AI cuts X-ray dose by two-thirds in angiography-guided procedures
milestones.summary: GenDSA-V2, trained on over 5 million images from 46,829 patients at 70 centres, generates angiography frames so fewer X-ray exposures are needed. In a blinded randomized trial of 1,068 patients undergoing procedures for brain aneurysms, lung cancer or liver cancer, mean air kerma fell from 457.4 to 151.3 mGy, with similar complications (7.5% vs 8.1%).

before_after.metric: Mean air kerma radiation dose per procedure

milestones.why_it_matters: Digital subtraction angiography guides over 100,000 procedures a day, exposing patients and staff to radiation. A prospectively validated low-dose method could cut cumulative exposure, especially for interventional teams.
organizations: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

milestones.title: Claude carries out a particle-theory calculation under a physicist's supervision
milestones.summary: Harvard's Matthew Schwartz steered Claude Opus 4.5, by text prompts only, to resum the Sudakov shoulder of the C-parameter in electron-positron collisions at NLL+NLO. Claude did the calculations, Monte Carlo checks and writing; Schwartz caught errors, including a wrong factorization formula, and validated the result. He estimates two weeks instead of about a year.

before_after.metric: Time for a second-year-graduate-level theory project (author's estimate)

milestones.why_it_matters: It shows a language model can carry out a real, checkable theoretical physics calculation when an expert steers it, which could free physicists for harder questions.
organizations: NSF Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions
milestones.contested_note: Not peer reviewed. Schwartz reports Claude was sloppy, adjusted parameters to make plots match, and first used a wrong factorization formula; he says expert checking of every step was essential.

sources.label: Anthropic guest post by M. Schwartz, 2026-03-23

milestones.title: AI resolves Erdős problem #728 with a Lean proof, essentially autonomously
milestones.summary: Erdős problem #728 on factorial divisibility was vaguely stated; once a precise version was agreed, Kevin Barreto ran GPT-5.2 Pro and Harmonic's Aristotle, which produced a Lean proof by 6 January 2026. It was described as the first Erdős problem resolved essentially autonomously by AI; Pomerance's 2014 paper uses a similar method.
milestones.why_it_matters: Marked the shift from AI rediscovering known results to AI producing new, machine-checked solutions to problems collected from one of the most prolific mathematicians.

sources.label: Sothanaphan, writeup of Aristotle's proof, arXiv:2601.07421
Tao et al., AI contributions to Erdős problems (wiki)

milestones.title: LLM agent runs multistage experiments on Berkeley's Advanced Light Source
milestones.summary: Berkeley Lab's Accelerator Assistant, an agent driven by large language models, turns plain-language requests into executable plans: retrieving archived data, finding control channels, writing scripts, operating the accelerator within safety limits and analyzing results. On the Advanced Light Source it cut experiment preparation about 100-fold versus an expert's manual scripting.

before_after.metric: time to prepare an experiment workflow
before_after.after: a few minutes from one prompt (about 100× faster)

milestones.why_it_matters: Big facilities lose scarce beam time to setup work. Agents that safely turn intent into machine operations could let scientists run more, and more complex, experiments.
ai_systems: Accelerator Assistant (LLM agent built on the Osprey framework)

milestones.title: Transformer model warns of emerging sunspot regions hours before they surface
milestones.summary: NASA's COFFIES team (NJIT, Princeton, NASA Ames) trained a sliding-window transformer on Solar Dynamics Observatory data from 46 active regions, looking for subtle acoustic-power and magnetic changes from flux rising below the surface. Forecasting up to 12 hours ahead, the published model caught emergence onset on average 9.24 hours early.

before_after.metric: Error (RMSE) of continuum-intensity forecasts at active-region emergence
before_after.after: 10.6% lower; onset flagged 9.24 h early on average

milestones.why_it_matters: Active regions launch the flares and coronal mass ejections that threaten satellites, power grids and astronauts. Warning hours before they appear would extend space-weather forecasts.
milestones.contested_note: Retrospective test on 46 active regions, not an operational forecast; lead times vary more than with the LSTM baseline. The January 2026 preprint reported a 4.73 h average lead.

sources.label: Tirona et al., JGR: Machine Learning and Computation, 2026-08-14

milestones.title: LLM chatbot takes patient histories before specialist visits in randomized trial
milestones.summary: PreA, a GPT-4o mini chatbot co-designed with patients and clinicians, took histories and drafted referral reports before specialist visits at two hospitals in western China. In a trial randomizing 2,069 patients across 24 specialties, it cut consultation time 28.7% (4.41 to 3.14 minutes) and raised physician-rated care coordination; unassisted use matched staff-assisted use.

before_after.metric: Specialist consultation time

milestones.why_it_matters: Specialists in crowded, under-resourced hospitals get minutes per patient. An AI that gathers the history and drafts the referral returns that time to examination and decisions.
organizations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
First Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical University
Affiliated Hospital of Gansu Medical College

milestones.title: 19 LLM agents and lab robots run closed-loop perovskite materials research
milestones.summary: MARS, from the Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, coordinates 19 language-model agents and 16 domain tools in orchestrator, scientist, engineer, executor and analyst groups that drive robotic experiments. It optimised perovskite nanocrystal synthesis within 10 iterations and designed a water-stable 'core-shell-corona' perovskite composite in 3.5 hours.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most self-driving labs tune one fixed recipe. Agents that also plan, pick tools and interpret results move automation toward labs that carry whole research projects.
ai_systems: MARS multi-agent and robot system (19 LLM agents, 16 tools)
organizations: Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
milestones.contested_note: Two demonstrations within one materials family, set up by the authors; details here rest on the abstract-level institute summary.

milestones.title: AISLE's AI analyzer credited with all 12 flaws in OpenSSL's Jan 2026 fixes
milestones.summary: OpenSSL's 27 January 2026 security advisory fixed 12 vulnerabilities, all reported by AISLE researchers (one also found independently by another researcher), who say their autonomous AI analyzer found them. One was high severity (a stack overflow in CMS message parsing), some date back to 1998, and AISLE's fixes were adopted for 5 of the 12.
milestones.why_it_matters: OpenSSL secures much of the internet's encrypted traffic and is heavily audited. An AI system finding every flaw in a release shows how far automated auditing has come.

milestones.title: AlphaGenome predicts regulatory effects of DNA variants from 1 million bases
milestones.summary: AlphaGenome reads 1 million bases of DNA and predicts thousands of functional genomic tracks at up to single-base resolution, including gene expression, chromatin accessibility, transcription-factor binding and splicing. Trained on human and mouse genomes, it matches or beats the strongest external models in 25 of 26 variant-effect evaluations.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most disease-linked DNA changes lie outside genes, in regulatory regions. One model scoring a variant across many layers of regulation helps researchers prioritize which changes matter.

sources.label: Google DeepMind blog, 2025-06-25 (preprint announcement; updated for Nature)

milestones.title: Perseverance drives Mars routes planned by generative AI for the first time
milestones.summary: NASA JPL used Anthropic's Claude vision-language models to analyse orbital images and terrain-slope data and write waypoints for Perseverance, a job human planners have done for 28 years. After checks on JPL's digital twin covering over 500,000 telemetry variables, the rover drove 210 m on 8 December 2025 and 246 m on 10 December.

before_after.metric: Who plans Mars rover routes
before_after.after: AI-generated waypoints; 210 m and 246 m driven

milestones.why_it_matters: Signal delays rule out joystick driving on Mars. Letting AI plan safe routes could mean longer drives, less operator workload and more science per day on distant worlds.
milestones.contested_note: Two demonstration drives. Rover drivers made minor changes using ground-level images Claude had not seen (Anthropic). Rovers already had onboard autonomous navigation; the first is generative-AI route planning.

milestones.title: AxiomProver proves Fel's conjecture with a formal Lean proof
milestones.summary: Axiom Math's AxiomProver, given a natural-language statement, produced a complete Lean/Mathlib proof of Fel's conjecture, an explicit formula for syzygy invariants of numerical semigroups. Axiom says no hints, helper lemmas or manual patches were added after kickoff; humans wrote the statement, definitions and the accompanying paper.
milestones.why_it_matters: An open conjecture went from statement to machine-checked proof without human mathematical input, so correctness rests on the Lean checker rather than trust in the AI.

milestones.title: Researchers log Gemini Deep Think helping settle open problems in theory
milestones.summary: Thirty-six researchers led from Google Research describe more than 15 cases where Gemini Deep Think helped resolve open questions, mostly in theoretical computer science, plus economics, optimisation and physics. Examples: a three-item counterexample refuting a 2015 online submodular welfare conjecture, and a fatal flaw it found in a cryptography preprint, confirmed by its authors.
milestones.why_it_matters: A documented record of what a model contributed, and which working habits made it useful, lets other researchers judge the claims and reuse the techniques.
ai_systems: Gemini Deep Think and advanced variants
milestones.contested_note: Section authors vouch only for their own sections; some results are partial, and most are not peer reviewed.

milestones.title: Sixteen Claude agents write a C compiler that builds the Linux kernel
milestones.summary: Nicholas Carlini ran 16 Claude Opus 4.6 agents in parallel, mostly unsupervised, over nearly 2,000 sessions and about $20,000 of API use. Without internet access they wrote a 100,000-line Rust C compiler that builds a bootable Linux 6.9 on x86, ARM and RISC-V and passes about 99% of most compiler test suites.
milestones.why_it_matters: A compiler is a large, tightly specified system. Agents building one from scratch show autonomous teams can deliver big, testable software; output slower than unoptimized GCC shows the limits.
milestones.contested_note: Anthropic lists limits: it calls GCC for 16-bit real-mode boot code, uses GCC's assembler and linker, and emits code slower than GCC with optimizations off. Chris Lattner (Modular, 2026-02-18) called it a competent textbook implementation tuned to pass tests rather than build general abstractions.

sources.label: Anthropic Engineering, Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes (2026-02-05)
Chris Lattner, The Claude C Compiler: what it reveals about the future of software (2026-02-18)

milestones.title: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 500+ high-severity bugs in heavily fuzzed open-source code
milestones.summary: Anthropic's red team ran Claude Opus 4.6 in a virtual machine with standard tools against open-source projects and validated more than 500 high-severity vulnerabilities, some missed for decades despite years of fuzzing. Examples in Ghostscript, OpenSC and the CGIF library are now patched by maintainers; human researchers validated each finding and wrote the first patches.
milestones.why_it_matters: Fuzzers miss bugs that need reasoning about code history or an algorithm's logic; finding them at scale helps under-resourced maintainers fix flaws before attackers find them.
milestones.contested_note: The 500+ count is Anthropic's own. Most reports were still in disclosure and the work focused on memory-corruption bugs, so the total cannot yet be checked independently.

sources.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, Evaluating and mitigating the growing risk of LLM-discovered 0-days (2026-02-05)

milestones.title: GPT-5 runs 36,000 lab experiments and cuts cell-free protein cost 40%
milestones.summary: GPT-5 designed, analysed and refined experiments run by Ginkgo Bioworks' robotic cloud lab, testing more than 36,000 cell-free protein synthesis recipes on over 580 plates in six rounds. Humans mainly prepared and loaded reagents and plates. It made the benchmark protein sfGFP at $422 per gram in reaction components, 40% below the previous best, $698.

before_after.metric: Specific cost of sfGFP by cell-free synthesis (20 µL reactions, 2 mL tubes)

milestones.why_it_matters: Cell-free protein synthesis makes proteins without living cells but is costly. A model that closes the loop with robots shows how labs could search recipe spaces too large for people.
milestones.contested_note: Not peer reviewed; one protein in one cell-free system. The cost counts reaction components only, not manufacturing, and R&D World notes yields depend strongly on oxygenation and reaction geometry.

milestones.title: Aletheia agent writes a research paper without human intervention
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's Aletheia, built on an advanced Gemini Deep Think, generates, checks and revises proofs in natural language. It wrote a paper on 'eigenweights' in arithmetic geometry with no human intervention. Run on 700 'open' Erdős problems, 137 of 200 gradable answers were flawed; of 13 meaningful ones, 4 were new and 9 already known.
milestones.why_it_matters: Moves AI from competition problems into the real research workflow of finding literature, proving and writing, with explicit accounting of what was autonomous.

milestones.title: GPT-5.2 conjectures formula showing single-minus gluon amplitudes are nonzero
milestones.summary: A preprint by Guevara, Lupsasca, Skinner, Strominger and Weil shows tree-level gluon amplitudes with one negative-helicity gluon, usually presumed zero, are nonzero in special 'half-collinear' kinematics. Per the paper, GPT-5.2 Pro first conjectured the key all-n formula, a new internal OpenAI model proved it, and the authors checked it by hand.

before_after.metric: single-minus tree-level gluon amplitudes
before_after.after: nonzero closed-form formula in half-collinear kinematics

milestones.why_it_matters: Scattering amplitudes are the core predictions of particle theory. A language model supplied the key conjecture and proof, though the result covers a narrow, unphysical-signature regime.
ai_systems: Internal OpenAI model (a scaffolded GPT-5.2, per OpenAI)
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer reviewed. D. Louapre (Hugging Face blog, 2026-02-19) calls the AI conjecture a real contribution but stresses the narrow scope (measure-zero kinematics in (2,2) signature), says the physics framing was human work, and says the AI workflow is under-documented.

milestones.title: AI workflow re-runs 384 political science papers to measure reproducibility
milestones.summary: Yiqing Xu (Stanford) and Leo Yang Yang (HKBU) built a Claude Code-coordinated workflow that fetches replication files, rebuilds environments, runs code and matches published regression tables, for about $2,000 in API costs. Across 384 sampled papers from three top journals, fully or largely reproducible papers rose from 20.8% before data-archiving rules to 82.5% after.

before_after.metric: Share of sampled papers fully or largely reproducible
before_after.after: 82.5% after (92.1% when replication files were accessible)

milestones.why_it_matters: Checking published results by hand is too slow to do at scale. Automated replication turns reproducibility from a spot check into something a whole field can measure.

milestones.title: Over 37,000 AI agents mine 55,984 trials for what makes drug targets succeed
milestones.summary: Stanford's Virtual Biotech, a team of AI agents organized like a drug company, annotated outcomes of 55,984 clinical trials and linked drug targets to single-cell data. Drugs aimed at cell-type-specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market and had 32% fewer adverse events, an association. It also proposed a lung cancer strategy targeting B7-H3.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most drugs fail in trials, often for reasons visible only across thousands of studies. Agent teams that can read and structure the whole trial record could steer target choice earlier and more cheaply.

milestones.title: Claude finds the construction for Knuth's Hamiltonian cycle problem
milestones.summary: Donald Knuth reported that Claude Opus 4.6, prompted and coached by Filip Stappers, found in about an hour a rule splitting the arcs of a digraph on m³ vertices into three Hamiltonian cycles for every odd m. Knuth wrote the proof, which Kim Morrison checked in Lean; GPT models later settled even m.

before_after.metric: Values of m with a known general decomposition
before_after.before: m = 3 proved; 4 ≤ m ≤ 16 found by computer search
before_after.after: All odd m (Claude's rule, proved); even m ≥ 8 soon after via GPT-5.3-codex and GPT-5.4 Pro

milestones.why_it_matters: One of computing's most respected figures, previously sceptical of generative AI, documented an AI solving a problem he had worked on for weeks.

milestones.title: AI agents write and formally verify a zlib-compatible compressor in Lean
milestones.summary: With loose human supervision, Claude-based coding agents wrote a zlib-format DEFLATE compressor and decompressor in the Lean language and proved, checked by Lean's kernel, that decompressing compressed data returns the original for every input and compression level (given a size limit). The proof spans over 1,100 theorems in about 32,000 lines.
milestones.why_it_matters: As AI writes more of the world's code, people need guarantees it is correct. Machine-checked proofs let anyone confirm the result without trusting the AI that produced it.

milestones.title: AI agent designs a Linux-capable RISC-V CPU from a 219-word spec in 12 hours
milestones.summary: Verkor's Design Conductor agent turned a 219-word requirements document into a verified, tape-out-ready layout of a Linux-capable RISC-V CPU in 12 hours, unaided. It met timing at 1.48 GHz in the ASAP7 7 nm academic kit and scored 3,261 on CoreMark, about a 2011 Intel Celeron. A May follow-up built an LLM accelerator.

before_after.metric: Time from specification to verified CPU layout
before_after.before: months to years for human teams

milestones.why_it_matters: Chip design takes large expert teams years. Agents that carry a specification all the way to a verified layout could make custom hardware cheap enough for many more uses.
ai_systems: Design Conductor (agent built on frontier LLMs)
milestones.contested_note: Company report. No chip was fabricated: verification was in simulation and layout used the predictive ASAP7 kit (IEEE Spectrum). The core is far simpler than leading-edge CPUs.

milestones.title: Viazovska's sphere-packing proofs in dimensions 8 and 24 formally verified
milestones.summary: Math Inc.'s Gauss joined a Lean project begun by Sidharth Hariharan and Maryna Viazovska, proving all remaining 8-dimensional results in five days (announced 23 February 2026), then formalized the 24-dimensional proof in about two weeks from the original paper alone. The roughly 200,000-line release also fixed a typo in the published paper.

before_after.metric: Lean formalization of optimal sphere packing

milestones.why_it_matters: First machine-checked verification of Fields Medal-winning work; the team had estimated six more months for dimension 8 alone with existing tools.

milestones.title: Machine learning on warming patterns cuts future-warming uncertainty by 70%
milestones.summary: Applied to large climate-model ensembles, machine learning found which grid cells' 1971-2020 warming trends best predict future global warming, mainly tropical and polar ones. Using the observed pattern cut projection error variance by about 70%, versus 48% with the global-mean trend, putting the chance of passing 2 °C by mid-century under SSP3-7.0 near 80%.

before_after.metric: Reduction in error variance of future global warming projections

milestones.why_it_matters: Policy hinges on how fast the world warms. Narrower projections tied to observed regional warming tell planners how soon Paris Agreement thresholds are likely to be crossed.
organizations: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology
Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium, University of Victoria

milestones.title: Evo 2 DNA model scores genetic variants without task-specific training
milestones.summary: Evo 2, from Arc Institute, NVIDIA and others, is a 40-billion-parameter DNA model trained on about 9 trillion bases with a 1-million-base context. It scores genetic variants, including BRCA1 variants, without task-specific training. Zero-shot human gene-essentiality prediction is modest (AUROC 0.66), within the range of simple conservation scores.
milestones.why_it_matters: A DNA model needing no per-task training could help read mutation effects in any species, though its own gene-essentiality result shows clear limits.

milestones.title: GPT-5.2 Pro helps show single-minus graviton amplitudes are also nonzero
milestones.summary: Three weeks after their gluon result, Guevara, Lupsasca, Skinner, Strominger and Weil showed that tree-level graviton amplitudes with one negative-helicity graviton, often presumed zero, are nonzero in special 'half-collinear' kinematics, deriving and solving a recursion for any number of gravitons. The paper says GPT-5.2 Pro and an internal OpenAI model played a significant role throughout.

before_after.metric: Single-minus tree-level graviton amplitudes
before_after.after: nonzero; recursion solved for any number of gravitons

milestones.why_it_matters: Gravity amplitudes are harder than gluon ones. Carrying the AI-assisted method over to gravitons suggests it generalizes, though the result holds only in a special kinematic regime.
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer reviewed. It extends the same team's February 2026 gluon result, criticised for its narrow kinematic scope; the regime needs Klein-space or complex momenta, and the paper does not itemize which steps the models did.

milestones.title: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 22 Firefox vulnerabilities in two weeks
milestones.summary: Working with Mozilla, Anthropic used Claude Opus 4.6 to scan nearly 6,000 Firefox C++ files. In two weeks it found bugs that led to 22 CVEs, 14 rated high severity, almost a fifth of the high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities fixed in 2025, plus 90 other bugs. Most fixes shipped in Firefox 148.
milestones.why_it_matters: Browsers are among the most attacked and most tested programs. Mozilla found the reports easy to reproduce, showing AI auditing adds value even to mature, heavily fuzzed code.

milestones.title: Conversational diagnostic AI AMIE talks with real patients before clinic visits
milestones.summary: At Beth Israel Deaconess, 98 urgent primary-care patients chatted with Google's AMIE before their visit while physicians supervised live. No safety stops were needed; supervisors noted one hallucination. AMIE's differential included the final diagnosis in 90% of cases (75% in its top three); evaluators rated its plans as safe as doctors' but less practical.
milestones.why_it_matters: Simulated wins do not show that AI is safe with real patients. This is a first supervised real-world step, small and single-arm, toward testing conversational diagnostic AI in randomized trials.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve raises lower bounds for nine classical Ramsey numbers
milestones.summary: Google researchers used AlphaEvolve to evolve search programs that build graphs with no large cliques or independent sets. They raised lower bounds for nine Ramsey numbers, such as R(3,13) from 60 to 61 and R(4,19) from 213 to 219, five in March and four more by April, and recovered every known exact lower bound.

before_after.metric: Lower bound on Ramsey number R(4,19)

milestones.why_it_matters: Ramsey records usually come from bespoke searches and can stand for years. One AI meta-method finding many improvements points to a general tool for extremal constructions, each easy to check.

sources.label: Nagda, Raghavan, Thakurta, Reinforced Generation of Combinatorial Structures: Ramsey Numbers, arXiv:2603.09172

milestones.title: Google rolls out AI urban flash-flood forecasts trained on news-derived data
milestones.summary: Google Research used Gemini to extract dated, located flood reports from news in 80 languages, building Groundsource: 2.6 million flash-flood records from over 150 countries. An LSTM model trained on it with global weather inputs forecasts urban flash floods up to 24 hours ahead on a 20 km grid, now rolling out on Flood Hub.

before_after.metric: Historical flash-flood records available for training

milestones.why_it_matters: Flash floods cause about 85% of flood deaths, often where gauges and radar are scarce. Forecasts built only from global data can reach cities that lack warning systems.
milestones.contested_note: Skill is measured against news-derived and GDACS records; Google says precision is underestimated because some floods go unreported, and much of Africa lacks enough ground truth to estimate accuracy.

sources.label: Google Research blog, urban flash flood forecasting, 2026-03-12
EarthArXiv preprint, AI expands urban flash flood forecasts, 2026-03-09

milestones.title: AI clears 64% of mammograms unread and finds more cancers, but recalls rise
milestones.summary: In a prospective paired trial of 31,301 women in Córdoba, Spain, treating exams Transpara rated low-risk as normal, unread, and double-reading the rest with AI support cut radiologist workload 63.6%. Cancer detection rose from 6.3 to 7.3 per 1,000, but recalls rose 14.8%, failing non-inferiority. AI-cleared exams included 11 cancers that standard reading found.

before_after.metric: Cancers detected per 1,000 women screened

milestones.why_it_matters: Shows in live screening that AI can take most normal exams off radiologists' desks while finding more cancers overall, the kind of evidence needed before AI reads unsupervised, though recalls rose.
organizations: Maimónides Biomedical Research Institute of Córdoba (IMIBIC)

milestones.title: AI agents run full particle-physics analyses on archived collider data
milestones.summary: MIT and CERN physicists gave Claude Code agents short prompts and open ALEPH, DELPHI and CMS data. Agents handled event selection, backgrounds, statistics and drafting, with humans signing off only at unblinding. They reproduced CMS's H→ττ signal strength within 0.16σ and made what the authors believe is the first Lund-plane measurement in electron-positron collisions.

before_after.metric: CMS 8 TeV H→ττ (μτh channel) signal strength

milestones.why_it_matters: Much of a collider analysis is repetitive code. Agents that carry it could free physicists for physics questions and reopen archived data from experiments that have shut down.
ai_systems: Claude Code with Claude Opus models
organizations: NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions
milestones.contested_note: The authors present demonstrations, not precision measurements: the agent's H→ττ uncertainty is nearly three times CMS's, and one ALEPH Z-width result sits 3.4σ low.

milestones.title: AI-assisted stroke decision support cuts repeat vascular events in 77 hospitals
milestones.summary: In a cluster-randomized trial across 77 Chinese hospitals (21,603 ischaemic stroke patients), a decision-support system combining AI imaging analysis, stroke-cause classification and guideline recommendations cut new vascular events at 3 months from 3.9% to 2.9% (HR 0.74), without more bleeding. Disability and mortality did not differ.

before_after.metric: New vascular event within 3 months

milestones.why_it_matters: Shows AI-based support can improve hard patient outcomes at scale in ordinary hospitals by helping clinicians apply proven treatments more consistently.
ai_systems: Stroke clinical decision support system with AI imaging analysis
organizations: Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University
China National Clinical Research Center for Neurological Diseases

milestones.title: RAVEN machine-learning pipeline validates 118 TESS planets, 31 newly found
milestones.summary: Warwick's RAVEN pipeline searched TESS full-frame images of over 2.2 million Sun-like stars for planets with 0.5-16 day orbits, using classifiers trained on simulated planets and false positives, then statistical validation. It validated 118 planets, 31 newly detected, and listed over 2,000 high-probability candidates, about 1,000 of them new.

before_after.metric: Uncertainty on close-in planet occurrence rates (companion RAVEN study)

milestones.why_it_matters: Uniformly vetted planets let astronomers measure how common planet types are. A companion study puts rare 'Neptunian desert' planets around just 0.08% of Sun-like stars.
ai_systems: RAVEN (machine-learning classifiers trained on simulated signals)
milestones.contested_note: Planets are statistically validated, not confirmed by mass measurements; the 2,000 high-probability candidates are not validated.

sources.label: Cui et al., MNRAS 546, stag022 (occurrence rates), 2026-01-07

milestones.title: Active learning finds electrolytes that triple lithium-metal cell lifetime
milestones.summary: A two-stage deep active learning framework chose which electrolyte formulations to test, modelling abrupt jumps between composition and performance, then transferred what it learned to new components with few extra measurements. After three learning rounds it found electrolytes that tripled the average lifetime of lithium-metal symmetric cells, and quickly improved Li||NMC811 full-cell formulations.

before_after.metric: Average lifetime of lithium-metal symmetric cells

milestones.why_it_matters: Lithium-metal anodes could greatly raise battery energy density but fail quickly. Finding long-lived electrolytes with few costly experiments eases a key bottleneck.
ai_systems: Deep kernel learning active-learning framework with knowledge transfer

milestones.title: Hurricane center's 2025 review ranks Google DeepMind's AI model among the best
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's experimental cyclone ensemble, shown live to US National Hurricane Center forecasters from June 2025, was assessed in NHC's official 2025 verification. Its ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly beat NHC's own Atlantic track forecasts at 12-72 hours, was the best Atlantic intensity model, and beat NHC's eastern Pacific track forecasts at 48-120 hours.

before_after.metric: Atlantic track skill at 12-72 h, 2025 season
before_after.before: NHC official forecast best of all guidance
before_after.after: GDMI slightly better than NHC official

milestones.why_it_matters: Hurricane track and strength decide who evacuates. An independent government review finding an AI model at or above expert forecasts is strong evidence it helps protect lives.
ai_systems: Google DeepMind Weather Lab experimental cyclone model (ensemble mean GDMI)

sources.label: Google DeepMind blog, Weather Lab launch, 2025-06-12

milestones.title: 30,000 Claude agents formalize a 500-page graduate textbook in Lean in a week
milestones.summary: Researchers at Meta FAIR and École des Ponts ran about 30,000 Claude 4.5 Opus agents in parallel on a shared code base to formalize Darij Grinberg's 500-plus-page graduate algebraic combinatorics textbook in Lean: 130,000 lines and 5,900 declarations, with all 340 target definitions and theorems formalized, in one week for about $100,000.
milestones.why_it_matters: Formalizing new research needs foundational texts in Lean faster than volunteers can write them; converting a whole graduate textbook automatically shows that bottleneck can be lifted.

sources.label: Gloeckle et al., Automatic Textbook Formalization, arXiv:2604.03071

milestones.title: Anthropic reports Claude Mythos Preview found thousands of zero-day bugs
milestones.summary: Anthropic said Claude Mythos Preview found thousands of high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities across every major operating system and browser, including a 27-year-old OpenBSD bug and a 16-year-old FFmpeg flaw, and wrote working exploits. Reviewers matched its severity ratings exactly in 89% of 198 checked reports; under 1% were patched at announcement.

before_after.metric: Working Firefox JavaScript-engine exploits in Anthropic's test harness (sandbox removed)

milestones.why_it_matters: AI that finds and weaponizes flaws at this scale shifts the balance between attackers and defenders, so Anthropic restricted access to organizations patching critical software (Project Glasswing).
milestones.contested_note: AISLE (blog, 2026-04-07) reported that small open-weight models, given the isolated vulnerable code, detected the flagship FreeBSD bug and, in one case, the core OpenBSD bug chain, arguing the capability is less exclusive than claimed. Most findings were undisclosed and unpatched, so the totals cannot yet be checked independently.

milestones.title: AAAI-26 gives every one of 22,977 submissions an AI peer review
milestones.summary: In the first conference-scale deployment of AI peer review, every AAAI-26 main-track paper got one labelled AI review alongside human reviews: 22,977 reviews in under a day, at under $1 each. Of 5,834 survey responses, 53.9% judged them useful versus 20.2% not; AI reviews rated better at spotting technical errors but more prone to nitpicking.

before_after.metric: Papers given an AI-generated review at one conference

milestones.why_it_matters: Submissions are outgrowing the supply of volunteer reviewers. Showing where AI reviews help at full scale, and where they fail, shapes how peer review copes.
ai_systems: AAAI-26 AI review system on GPT-5 (high reasoning, code execution, web search)
milestones.contested_note: Survey respondents self-selected. They also judged AI reviews more likely to overemphasise minor issues and to contain technical errors, and weak at judging novelty and significance.

milestones.title: Autonomous humanoid robot runs a half marathon faster than the human record
milestones.summary: At the Beijing E-Town humanoid robot half marathon, Honor's 'Lightning' covered the 21.1 km course in 50 minutes 26 seconds using autonomous navigation, beating the men's world record of 57:20. The 2025 winner, a remote-controlled robot, took 2 hours 40 minutes. About 300 robots from over 100 teams took part.

before_after.metric: Fastest robot half-marathon time

milestones.why_it_matters: Running fast for an hour without falling or getting lost tests balance, endurance, cooling and navigation together. A roughly threefold gain in a year shows how fast humanoid robots are improving.
ai_systems: Autonomous navigation and locomotion control (Honor 'Lightning' humanoid)
milestones.contested_note: The robot needed a battery change at 10.6 km (Honor, via Sixth Tone), and much of the speed gain came from joint and cooling hardware. Ars Technica notes it does not imply real-world uses.

milestones.title: Machine-learning-assisted search finds 10,091 new TESS planet candidates
milestones.summary: The T16 project detrended 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 light curves for stars down to magnitude 16, then searched them with random-forest classifiers and manual vetting. It found 11,554 transiting-planet candidates, 10,091 new, more than doubling known TESS candidates; radial-velocity follow-up confirmed one as a new hot Jupiter around TIC 183374187.

before_after.metric: Known TESS planet candidates

milestones.why_it_matters: Most planet searches skip faint stars. Opening them up gives far larger samples for measuring how common planets are, plus a long target list for follow-up.
milestones.contested_note: Candidates are not confirmed planets; only one has been confirmed so far.

sources.label: Roth et al., Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series 284:19, 2026-04-28

milestones.title: Firefox 150 ships fixes for 271 bugs found with Claude Mythos Preview
milestones.summary: Mozilla's Firefox 150, released 21 April 2026, fixed 271 security bugs that its pipeline found with an early Claude Mythos Preview: 180 rated sec-high, 80 moderate and 11 low, including a 20-year-old XSLT memory bug and several sandbox escapes. Firefox 148 had fixed 22 security bugs found with Claude Opus 4.6.

before_after.metric: Security bugs found with Claude and fixed in one Firefox release

milestones.why_it_matters: A heavily fuzzed, mature browser shipped hundreds of AI-found security fixes in one release, showing defenders can now use these models to harden critical code at scale.
milestones.contested_note: Severity ratings rest on crash symptoms, not confirmed exploits. Advisory MFSA 2026-30 groups internally found bugs into rollup CVEs, so the 271 do not appear individually; Mozilla's 7 May post reconciles the counts.

sources.label: Mozilla Hacks, Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview (2026-05-07)

milestones.title: Materials agent ElementsClaw guides discovery of four new superconductors
milestones.summary: Alibaba DAMO Academy, Renmin University and Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers built ElementsClaw, an agent pairing a 1-billion-parameter atomic model with language-model reasoning. It flagged 68,000 high-confidence superconductor candidates among 2.4 million crystals in 28 GPU hours. Synthesis confirmed four new superconductors, including Zr3ScRe8 (Tc 6.5 K) and HfZrRe4 (5.9 K).
milestones.why_it_matters: Generative models propose millions of materials, but choosing what to make is the bottleneck. An agent that ranks candidates and explains its picks turned predictions into verified superconductors.
organizations: Institute of Physics, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer reviewed; company-led. All four are rhenium-rich intermetallics in a system with known superconductors, with transition temperatures of 2.5-6.5 K, far below practical levels.

milestones.title: Machine learning raises use of essential medicines across Sierra Leone
milestones.summary: Working with Sierra Leone's government, researchers built a decision-aware machine-learning system that allocates scarce essential medicines to health facilities from sparse data. A staggered nationwide rollout raised consumption of allocated products by an estimated 19% in treated districts. The tool now covers about two million women and children under five.

before_after.metric: Consumption of allocated essential medicines
before_after.after: +19% in districts using the ML tool

milestones.why_it_matters: In low-income health systems, medicines often sit unused in one clinic while another runs out. Cheap software that allocates stock better can widen access without new supplies.
organizations: Sierra Leone National Medical Supplies Agency
Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation

milestones.title: Pathology agent system proposes and tests its own tumour measurements
milestones.summary: SPARK, a multi-agent system from Cologne-led researchers, turns biological ideas into image-analysis tools on tissue slides without extra model training, then tests them. Across 18 cohorts, five cancer types and more than 5,400 patients, its self-generated concepts correlated with survival, known pathology variables and predictive biomarkers.
milestones.why_it_matters: Pathology AI usually measures features people chose in advance. An agent that proposes and tests its own measurable ideas could surface tumour biology nobody thought to look for.
ai_systems: SPARK (System of Pathology Agents for Research and Knowledge)
milestones.contested_note: Retrospective cohorts only; the authors say prospective validation is needed before clinical use.

sources.label: Trost et al., Nature Medicine 32:2254, online 2026-04-29

milestones.title: GPT-5.4 Pro output yields new method resolving Erdős primitive-set problems
milestones.summary: An autonomous GPT-5.4 Pro run produced the first proof of Erdős problem #1196 in April 2026. Alexeev, Barreto, Lichtman, Price, Tao and coauthors turned its idea, Markov chains with von Mangoldt weights, into a method proving #1196 and #1217, a short proof of the Erdős Primitive Set Conjecture and a revised Banks–Martin conjecture.
milestones.why_it_matters: An AI-suggested idea, overlooked since Erdős's 1935 paper, became a reusable method settling several problems at once: AI contributing technique, not just answers.

milestones.title: Unsupervised machine learning spots foreshock patterns before large quakes
milestones.summary: GFZ-led researchers used unsupervised machine learning to sort catalogued earthquakes into clustered families and categories. Before the Kahramanmaraş (2023), Iquique (2014) and L'Aquila (2009) earthquakes, a 'critical' category of long-lasting families appeared weeks to months ahead. For Noto (2024) and Amatrice (2016), which had no known precursors, it found none.
milestones.why_it_matters: Whether big earthquakes announce themselves is a central open question. A method that flags preparatory phases without preset rules, and stays silent otherwise, could feed operational forecasting.
milestones.contested_note: Retrospective test on five earthquakes, not a forecast; the authors note it cannot detect quakes that lack a seismic preparatory phase.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve cuts Spanner write amplification 20% and software size nearly 9%
milestones.summary: A year after launch, Google DeepMind reported that AlphaEvolve refined the compaction heuristics of Spanner, Google's global database, cutting write amplification by 20%, and found compiler strategies that shrank software's storage footprint by nearly 9%. It is now a regular tool in TPU design and found cache policies in two days rather than months.

before_after.metric: Spanner write amplification

milestones.why_it_matters: Writing less data per request means longer-lasting drives and lower costs in one of the world's largest databases. AI-found optimizations are becoming routine production engineering.

milestones.title: Machine-learning-designed electrolyzer channel raises current density 23%
milestones.summary: Tsinghua University engineers used a mixture-of-experts machine-learning surrogate, instead of simulating every geometry with fluid dynamics, to search flow-channel designs that clear gas bubbles in water electrolyzers. A prototype with the AI-chosen array-type channel delivered about 23% more current density at 2 V than a conventional serpentine design, and the gain held in scaled-up devices.

before_after.metric: Current density at 2 V

milestones.why_it_matters: Green hydrogen is costly partly because trapped bubbles waste energy in electrolyzers. A better channel geometry is a cheap hardware change that gets more hydrogen from the same voltage.

sources.label: Zhang et al., Science Advances 12, eadz1865, 2026-05-08

milestones.title: OpenAI model disproves Erdős's 1946 unit distance conjecture
milestones.summary: An internal OpenAI model constructed, in one shot, planar point sets with at least n^(1+δ) unit-distance pairs (fixed δ>0, infinitely many n), refuting Erdős's 1946 conjecture of n^(1+o(1)). The proof uses infinite class field towers. Nine mathematicians including Alon, Gowers and Tsimerman published a checked, simplified version; humans soon improved the exponent.

before_after.metric: Max unit distances among n planar points (lower bound)
before_after.before: n^(1+c/log log n), believed optimal since 1946

milestones.why_it_matters: Gowers wrote he would have recommended it to the Annals of Mathematics without hesitation; it overturned an 80-year-old belief in discrete geometry using number theory few expected to apply.

sources.label: OpenAI, Planar point sets with many unit distances (2026-05-20)
Alon, Bloom, Gowers et al., Remarks on the disproof

milestones.title: Formal proof-search agents resolve 9 open Erdős problems in Lean
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind evaluated LLM agents that write Lean proofs on open problems at scale. The strongest autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems with Lean statements, at a few hundred dollars each, and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures; a simpler generate-and-check agent matched the Erdős results but cost more on the hardest problems.
milestones.why_it_matters: Every claimed solution is machine-checked, so AI results can be trusted at scale and low cost, turning plausible text into guaranteed proofs.

milestones.title: Neural network trained on one tokamak forecasts plasma bursts on another
milestones.summary: A network trained only on megahertz turbulence measurements from 1,400 DIII-D discharges forecasts the onset of Type-I edge-localized modes, damaging plasma bursts, with true-positive rates above 80% on DIII-D. Applied to the Korean KSTAR tokamak with no retraining, it still forecast onsets, and explainability tools showed it tracked physical instability drivers.

before_after.metric: Retraining needed to forecast ELMs on a different tokamak

milestones.why_it_matters: Future reactors such as ITER will have little data to train on before they must be protected. Models that carry over between machines could guard them from the first day.
milestones.contested_note: Tested on archived discharges; the authors leave real-time use to future work.

milestones.title: Parisi and Zamponi prove a 2014 jamming conjecture with Claude's help
milestones.summary: Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi proved analytically that two jamming exponents satisfy a + b = 1, a relation seen numerically since 2014 but never proved, yielding scaling laws predicted by Wyart's marginal-stability arguments. The paper says the proof came through interaction with Claude (Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.7) and was verified by the authors.

before_after.metric: Status of the identity a + b = 1 for jamming exponents

milestones.why_it_matters: Jamming governs how sand, foams and glasses become rigid. The proof ties replica theory to marginal-stability arguments, and a Nobel laureate credits an AI model with the key idea.
milestones.contested_note: Zamponi told Live Science that Claude's first output contained errors needing revision but its core idea was correct; about 40 prompts led to the verified proof.

milestones.title: GPT-5.5 Pro helps improve the high-dimensional lattice packing bound
milestones.summary: Abuya, Gargava and Zhao proved lattice sphere packings of density at least c·N²·log log N·2^(−N) in infinitely many dimensions N, beating Klartag's bound by a log log N factor. Prompted by Zhao, GPT-5.5 Pro proposed the approach and proved the bound; the other two authors had pursued a similar idea, and all three verified it.

before_after.metric: Lattice packing density lower bound

milestones.why_it_matters: Dense high-dimensional packings underpin coding theory and lattice cryptography; an AI combined two leading techniques into a result experts then checked.

milestones.title: Deep learning reads plant regulatory DNA in Arabidopsis and transfers to maize
milestones.summary: One neural network trained on 568 Arabidopsis DNA-binding datasets covering 46 transcription-factor families predicts where regulators bind DNA. Of 7,364 trait-linked variants, 20.72% were predicted to gain or lose binding sites; reporter assays on 340 constructs supported several predictions. The model also transferred to maize heat-stress data.
milestones.why_it_matters: Many crop-trait variants sit in regulatory DNA, not genes. Predicting how they alter transcription-factor binding could help pinpoint causal variants, even in species with little data.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research

milestones.title: Autonomous catalysis lab finds rhodium catalyst conditions 2.5 times faster
milestones.summary: Flex-Cat couples parallel pressurized mini-reactors with Bayesian optimization over ligands and process conditions. In 680 autonomous experiments on rhodium-catalysed propylene hydroformylation it found ligand-condition regions with over 2.5-fold higher turnover frequency, widened the regioselectivity range, and found ligands whose selectivity flips with conditions; top hits were validated at 10-fold volume.

before_after.metric: Turnover frequency in propylene hydroformylation

milestones.why_it_matters: Hydroformylation is a major industrial route to aldehydes. Running pressurized gas-liquid catalysis autonomously, with an industrial partner and scale-up checks, moves self-driving labs toward real processes.
organizations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

milestones.title: Active-learning lab finds 3D-printable alloys that resist heat and oxidation
milestones.summary: University of Toronto researchers paired active learning with laser 3D printing to search nickel-cobalt-chromium compositions. In a few weeks they found six printable alloys up to about 40% harder than equiatomic NiCoCr; Ni12Co62Cr26 kept about 50% more hardness at 600 °C, and Ni36Co14Cr50 cut oxidation mass gain by 85% at 1,000 °C versus conventional superalloys.

before_after.metric: Oxidation mass gain at 1,000 °C

milestones.why_it_matters: Jet engines and power plants need printable metals that survive heat. Finding them with few experiments, far from the usual equal-part recipes, shortens alloy development.

sources.label: Talbot et al., npj Advanced Manufacturing, 2026-06-23

milestones.title: Deep learning reveals a new ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death
milestones.summary: Trained on every ECG in a Swedish region linked to death records, a deep-learning model flagged 2.2% of patients with a 7.0% annual sudden-death rate, above those with weak heart pumping (4.6%); 86.1% were missed by that standard test. A generative model exposed the visible waveform feature driving it. US and Taiwanese cohorts validated it.

before_after.metric: Annual sudden cardiac death rate in flagged group

milestones.why_it_matters: Defibrillators prevent sudden death, but today's main criterion misses most victims. An easily visible ECG marker found by AI could better target who receives one, pending prospective trials.
ai_systems: Deep-learning ECG risk model with a generative ECG waveform model
organizations: University of Chicago Booth School of Business
University of Gothenburg / Sahlgrenska University Hospital

milestones.title: Neural networks design proteins that bind two drugs, with 100% and 83% success
milestones.summary: Dana-Farber and Harvard researchers paired two neural networks in a design loop to make proteins from scratch that bind two chemically distinct drugs, exatecan and apixaban, with success rates of 100% and 83%. The tightest had picomolar-to-nanomolar affinity; an optimized exatecan binder protected the drug's labile lactone ring from hydrolysis for days.

before_after.metric: Affinity of tightest binder versus next-leading method

milestones.why_it_matters: Proteins that grab small molecules can deliver drugs, sense them or catalyze reactions. Zero-shot design with high success cuts the trial and error that limited earlier methods.

milestones.title: Herculaneum scroll's surviving text virtually unrolled and read end to end
milestones.summary: Using phase-contrast X-ray scans from ESRF's BM18 beamline, computational unrolling and machine-learning ink detection, a Vesuvius Challenge, University of Kentucky and ESRF team read all surviving text of PHerc. 1667, the core left by failed openings: about 1.4 metres of papyrus, the lower parts of some 22 columns of Greek, likely a Stoic ethical treatise.

before_after.metric: Extent read of a rolled Herculaneum papyrus
before_after.after: all surviving text, about 22 partial columns

milestones.why_it_matters: Moves scroll reading from demonstrations to a repeatable method; the same work identified another roll as Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8, pointing to systematic recovery of the unopened library.

milestones.title: OpenAI model proves the 50-year-old cycle double cover conjecture
milestones.summary: OpenAI released a three-page proof, credited entirely to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, that every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles covering each edge exactly twice, a 1970s conjecture of Tutte, Itai and Rodeh, Szekeres and Seymour. Sang-il Oum and Jim Geelen wrote expositions, Johannes Carmesin confirmed it, and Lean formalizations exist.
milestones.why_it_matters: One of graph theory's best-known open problems fell to a short argument built on classical flow theorems, suggesting some famous conjectures are hard to spot rather than deep.
milestones.contested_note: Correctness is not disputed. Thomas Bloom noted that using nowhere-zero F₂³-flows on cubic graphs to study cycle double covers goes back at least to Bermond, Jackson and Jaeger (1983).

sources.label: OpenAI, A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture (PDF, 2026-07-10)
Johannes Carmesin, The cycle double cover theorem, The Matroid Union (2026-07-21)

milestones.title: Claude Fable 5 finds a counterexample to the 1939 Jacobian conjecture
milestones.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a degree-7 polynomial map in three variables, credited to Claude Fable 5, whose Jacobian determinant is the constant −2 yet which is generically three-to-one, so it has no inverse.
