This disproves the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension above two; the two-variable case remains open.
milestones.why_it_matters: An 87-year-old conjecture, the target of many failed proofs, was settled by a machine-found example that anyone can check with computer algebra in seconds.
milestones.contested_note: The counterexample is not disputed, but how it was found has not been disclosed. Adrian Vasiu said an AI-written exposition borrowed notation and ideas from an unpublished Borisov–Gabber–Vasiu draft; Alpöge later said their method deserves credit too (Wikipedia).

sources.label: Terence Tao, A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample (2026-07-21)
The Conversation, 'hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx' (2026-07-22)

milestones.title: AI helps specialists predict genetic causes of inherited blindness in trial
milestones.summary: Retina4IRD predicts 17 genotype categories of inherited retinal disease from retinal photographs and scans. In a multicentre trial randomizing 300 patients with suspected disease, specialists using it named the gene group confirmed by sequencing within their top five guesses for 88.5% of patients, versus 67.3% for specialists alone; top-one accuracy rose from 22.4% to 37.8%.

before_after.metric: Top-5 genetic diagnosis accuracy

milestones.why_it_matters: Inherited retinal diseases need gene-specific care and trials, but genetic testing is slow and scarce. Image-based AI can point specialists to likely genes earlier and guide which tests to order.
organizations: Shanghai General Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

milestones.title: Claude Mythos Preview finds new attacks on HAWK signatures and 7-round AES
milestones.summary: Anthropic reported two attacks found largely by Claude Mythos Preview. A lattice symmetry cuts expected key recovery for HAWK-256, challenge parameters of a NIST post-quantum signature candidate, from 2^64 to 2^38 operations. A new meet-in-the-middle attack on 7-round AES-128 runs 200–800 times faster than the best before. Full AES is unaffected.

before_after.metric: Expected key-recovery cost for HAWK-256

milestones.why_it_matters: Encryption standards rest on years of expert attack. An AI weakening a post-quantum candidate in about 60 hours of work shows such review can be greatly accelerated before deployment.

Philip Arathoon, Gavin Ball and Matthew Kvalheim give five positive charges, three on a triangle and two small ones on its axis, with at least 24 non-degenerate equilibria, above the bound of 16. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol suggested the construction; the authors verified it.

before_after.metric: Most equilibria known for five positive charges

milestones.why_it_matters: A claim from a classic 1873 physics treatise falls to a construction an AI suggested. The three- and four-charge cases remain open.

milestones.title: Claude proves over two thirds of zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line
milestones.summary: Asked by a non-mathematician to attack the Riemann hypothesis, an unreleased Claude model running about 60 subagents proved that over two thirds (67.25%) of zeta's nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line, up from 5/12. milestones.why_it_matters: The share of zeros proven on the critical line is a standard yardstick of progress toward the Riemann hypothesis; this moves it past two thirds, though it does not lead to a proof.

milestones.title: Agent-driven hackathon re-tests a third of ICML 2026's accepted papers

milestones.contested_note: Verdicts come from an AI judge reading agent logbooks; 502 papers had only toy-scale evidence, and some claimed falsifications were reproduction bugs, so organisers re-checked them (Hugging Face blog).

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve helps lower the matrix multiplication exponent to ω < 2.371177

before_after.metric: Upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent ω

milestones.why_it_matters: ω sets the asymptotic cost of multiplying matrices and of the many algorithms that reduce to it; each small improvement has taken years of human work.

milestones.why_it_matters: One of mathematics' deepest proofs is now checked line by line by computer, suggesting AI can make verifying frontier mathematics routine.

milestones.title: AI-assisted, Lean-checked proofs show forced 3D Euler flows can blow up
milestones.summary: Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) posted proofs that the 3D incompressible Euler equations, the 2D Boussinesq system and the porous-medium equation can form finite-time singularities under a smooth external force, extending Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa's method. Claude and OpenAI's Codex helped heavily; Claude wrote all the Lean, which uses only standard axioms.
milestones.why_it_matters: Blow-up for the frictionless Euler equations is a recognized stepping stone toward the Navier–Stokes Millennium problem, and here the whole argument is machine-checked.
milestones.contested_note: Not peer-reviewed. Terence Tao called it a remarkable achievement with significant AI input, released earlier than planned because of external events. The force is an added ingredient; the unforced problem stays open.

milestones.title: Neural-network search finds a candidate stable blow-up for unforced 3D Euler
milestones.summary: Anima Anandkumar's Caltech group used a physics-informed neural network, steered away from trivial solutions and refined with splines for certified error bounds, to find an approximate self-similar blow-up of the 3D Euler equations in free space, with no boundary or force. It appears numerically stable; a rigorous stability proof is still missing.
milestones.why_it_matters: Unforced blow-up in free space is the version fluid experts care most about; a precise, stable candidate is the usual first step toward a computer-assisted proof.
milestones.contested_note: Terence Tao (Mathstodon, 2026-09-08): a promising candidate that appears numerically stable, but a rigorous demonstration of stability is still lacking and may need enormous effort.

milestones.title: OpenAI claims Lean-checked forced blow-up for Navier–Stokes, a Clay problem

milestones.title: AI-guided lab finds iridium-free catalysts for acidic water splitting
milestones.summary: Lila Sciences' human-supervised closed-loop platform, over 90% automated, combined sputter synthesis, high-throughput screening, machine-learning models and language-model reasoning to test 2,942 catalysts across 53 material systems. milestones.title: Exact fold carries a loose ball-and-rod crystal into the densest packing
milestones.subfield: discrete geometry; rigidity theory; sphere packing
milestones.summary: A framework of balls joined by rigid rods, arranged like the boron net of calcium hexaboride, folds continuously into the densest stacking of equal balls. No rod stretches and no balls overlap, while density rises steadily from 0.2233 to 0.7405 (pi/sqrt18). An explicit formula and an exact certificate of 16,240 nonnegative coefficients cover every instant.

before_after.metric: Highest packing density reached by a rod-preserving motion of this framework

milestones.why_it_matters: A floppy, mostly empty scaffold can reach the densest possible packing by folding alone. An AI search found a path in about 11 minutes; an exact proof followed the next day.
